questions.stem: Work out $\dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{2}{5}$. Give your answer in its simplest form.
markscheme: M1: multiplies numerators and denominators ($\dfrac{6}{20}$ seen)
questions.modelAnswer: Multiply across: $\dfrac{3 \times 2}{4 \times 5} = \dfrac{6}{20}$. Cancelling by 2 gives $\dfrac{3}{10}$. Answer: $\dfrac{3}{10}$.

questions.stem: Work out the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon.
questions.modelAnswer: A hexagon has 6 sides, so the interior angles sum to $(6 - 2) \times 180^\circ = 4 \times 180^\circ = 720^\circ$.

questions.stem: A fair spinner has 8 equal sections: 3 are red, 3 are blue and 2 are green. The spinner is spun once. Work out the probability that it lands on green.
markscheme: M1: identifies 2 favourable outcomes out of 8 equally likely outcomes
questions.modelAnswer: Two of the eight equally likely sections are green, so the probability is $\dfrac{2}{8} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.
The highest common factor of $6x^2$ and $9x$ is $3x$, so $6x^2 - 9x = 3x(2x - 3)$. Both brackets share no further factor, so this is fully factorised.

questions.stem: Make $x$ the subject of the formula $y = 3x - 2$.
markscheme: M1: adds 2 to both sides ($y + 2 = 3x$ seen)

questions.stem: The masses, in kilograms, of eight parcels are: $4, 7, 2, 9, 5, 5, 11, 3$. Work out the median mass.
markscheme: M1: orders the eight values correctly
M1: identifies the 4th and 5th values ($5$ and $5$) as the middle pair
questions.modelAnswer: Ordered: $2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9, 11$. With eight values the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: $\dfrac{5 + 5}{2} = 5$ kg.

questions.stem: An L-shaped garden plot is made from a large rectangle measuring $8$ m by $5$ m with a rectangular corner measuring $3$ m by $2$ m removed. Work out the area of the plot.
markscheme: M1: valid method (subtract the cut-out from the large rectangle, or split into two rectangles)
M1: correct area of the large rectangle ($40$ m$^2$)
M1: correct area of the removed corner ($6$ m$^2$)
questions.modelAnswer: Large rectangle: $8 \times 5 = 40$ m$^2$. Removed corner: $3 \times 2 = 6$ m$^2$. Plot area: $40 - 6 = 34$ m$^2$.

questions.stem: The price of a train ticket increases by $10\%$ and then, six months later, decreases by $10\%$. Work out the overall percentage change from the original price. State clearly whether it is an increase or a decrease.
markscheme: A1: states it is an overall decrease
questions.modelAnswer: The combined multiplier is $1.1 \times 0.9 = 0.99$, so the final price is $99\%$ of the original — an overall decrease of $1\%$. The two changes do not cancel because the second percentage acts on the larger, increased price.
